title: Cicoria Ripassata
instructions:
Cicoria Ripassata

Roman-style chicory boiled, squeezed dry, and sautéed with garlic, chile, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 2 1/4 lb chicory
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 garlic cloves, sliced
1 small chile, sliced
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Trim the chicory, removing tough stems and damaged leaves.

2. Wash repeatedly in cold water until no grit remains.

3. Bring a large pot of water to a boil with about 2/3 teaspoon salt.

4. Boil the chicory for 8–10 minutes, until tender but still green.

5. Drain and cool slightly.

6. Squeeze very well by hand to remove excess water.

7. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet.

8. Add the garlic and chile and cook for 1 minute.

9. Add the chicory.

10. Sauté over high heat for about 5 minutes, stirring often.

11. Add the remaining salt.

Service

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

Squeezing the chicory thoroughly prevents residual water from diluting the oil and turning the sauté into steaming.

title: Puntarelle alla Romana
instructions:
Puntarelle alla Romana

Crisp Roman puntarelle with anchovy, garlic, vinegar, and extra-virgin olive oil dressing.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 1 1/3 lb cleaned puntarelle
6 oil-packed anchovy fillets
1 garlic clove
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp white-wine vinegar
1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/8 tsp fine salt
about 2 lb ice for soaking

Preparation

1. Remove the tough outer leaves and woody base.

2. Cut the inner shoots lengthwise into very thin strips.

3. Fill a bowl with very cold water and ice.

4. Soak the strips for 1 hour so they curl and become crisp.

5. Meanwhile, crush the garlic and anchovies into a paste.

6. Add the vinegar and mix.

7. Whisk in the olive oil gradually.

8. Add the pepper and only a small pinch of salt.

9. Drain the puntarelle.

10. Dry them thoroughly in a salad spinner or clean towel.

11. Toss with the dressing immediately before serving.

Service

Serve cold and crisp.

Chef's note

Dry the puntarelle thoroughly. Residual water breaks the dressing and prevents it from coating the vegetables.

instructions:
Beans with Pork Rind

Roman-style cannellini beans with cured pork rind, tomato, onion, garlic, and cured ham fat.

Yield: 4 servings

about 1/4 lb cured pork rind
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp tomato passata

1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Soak the cannellini beans in cold water for 12 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Cook the beans in the measured water at a gentle boil for 60–90 minutes, until tender.

4. Trim excess fat from the pork rind and singe off any remaining hairs.

5. Cut into pieces.

6. Boil the rind for 30 minutes and drain.

7. Put the onion, 1 garlic clove, cured ham fat, olive oil, and parsley in a saucepan.

8. Cook over medium-low heat for 7 minutes.

9. Add the passata and cook for 20 minutes.

10. Add the beans and pork rind.

11. Cook together for another 10 minutes.

12. Season with salt and pepper.

Service

Serve very hot with rustic bread.

Chef's note

Boil the pork rind before adding it to the sauce so it becomes tender and releases gelatin without making the dish excessively heavy.

instructions:
Vignarola Romana

Roman spring vegetables with artichokes, peas, fava beans, lettuce, scallions, and pancetta.

Yield: 4 servings

about 4 cups chopped romaine lettuce
2 scallions, sliced
1/3 cup diced pancetta or guanciale
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 lemon
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Fill a bowl with cold water and lemon juice.

2. Trim the artichokes, removing tough outer leaves and tips.

3. Halve them, remove any choke, and cut into wedges.

4. Put them in the acidulated water.

5. Shell the peas and fava beans.

6. Wash and coarsely chop the lettuce.

7. Heat the olive oil in a wide pan.

8. Add the scallions and pancetta.

9. Cook for 5 minutes.

10. Drain the artichokes and add them with the peas and fava beans.

11. Season with salt and pepper.

12. Cover and cook gently for 10 minutes without adding water.

13. Add the lettuce.

14. Cover again and cook for another 15 minutes.

Service

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

Vignarola cooks in the natural moisture released by the vegetables. Added water would dilute their flavor.

2. Trim the ends.

3. Cut into rounds about 3/16 inch thick.

6. Drain on paper towels.

7. Arrange one layer of zucchini in a container.

9. Repeat the layers until all ingredients are used.

10. Cover.

11. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes before serving.

Chef's note

Fry only a small batch at a time so the oil stays hot and the zucchini does not absorb excessive fat.

title: Melanzane a Funghetto
instructions:
Melanzane a Funghetto

Neapolitan eggplant cubes fried and quickly sautéed with garlic and parsley.

Yield: 2 servings

Ingredients

1 large dark eggplant, about 1 lb
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 garlic clove, crushed
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1 tsp fine salt, divided
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Cut the eggplant lengthwise into four wedges.

2. Remove the seedy center.

3. Cut the remaining flesh into 3/4-inch cubes.

4. Put the cubes in a colander.

5. Sprinkle with about 2/3 teaspoon salt.

6. Rest for 30 minutes.

7. Squeeze lightly and pat dry.

8. Heat about 1/3 cup olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.

9. Fry the eggplant in small batches until golden, about 4–5 minutes.

10. Drain.

11. Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil with the garlic in a second skillet.

12. Add the eggplant and sauté over high heat for 2 minutes.

13. Remove the garlic.

14. Add the pepper, parsley, and remaining salt.

Service

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

The preliminary salting draws out moisture so the cubes brown more readily without collapsing.

Scarola alla Napoletana

Neapolitan escarole with olives, anchovies, capers, raisins, pine nuts, garlic, and chile.

2 oil-packed anchovy fillets
1 tbsp salt-packed capers, rinsed
1 garlic clove

1 pinch dried chile

Preparation

1. Remove the core and any damaged outer leaves.

2. Wash the escarole thoroughly.

3. Heat the olive oil in a very wide skillet.

4. Add the garlic, anchovies, and capers.

5. Cook for 2 minutes, until the anchovies begin to dissolve.

6. Add the chile and raisins.

7. Add the escarole while still slightly damp.

8. Cover.

9. Cook over low heat for about 20 minutes.

10. Meanwhile, toast the pine nuts in a dry skillet for 2 minutes.

11. Add the olives to the escarole.

12. Uncover and cook until the pan juices are nearly dry.

13. Taste and add salt only if necessary.

14. Add the pine nuts.

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

Escarole releases enough moisture to cook covered. Do not add extra liquid unless the pan is truly in danger of scorching.

title: Sicilian Roasted Artichokes
instructions:
Sicilian Roasted Artichokes

Sicilian artichokes slowly grilled over coals with garlic, parsley, olive oil, and salt.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

8 artichokes
4 garlic cloves, minced
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 small chile, minced, optional
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 lemon
1/2 cup water for basting

Preparation

1. Trim the stems, leaving about 3/4 inch attached.

2. Gently tap the artichoke heads on a cutting board to open the leaves like flowers.

3. Fill a basin with cold water and lemon juice.

4. Wash the artichokes in the acidulated water.

5. Mix the garlic, parsley, optional chile, 6 tablespoons olive oil, and salt.

6. Work the seasoning between the leaves of each artichoke.

7. Prepare hot stable coals with no active flames.

8. Arrange the artichokes on the grill or close to the coals.

9. Cook slowly for about 30 minutes, turning regularly.

10. Mix the water with the remaining olive oil.

11. Lightly baste the artichokes during cooking.

12. When the hearts are tender and the outer leaves are deeply charred, remove from the grill.

13. Cool for 5 minutes.

Service

Discard any completely burned outer leaves and serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

The coals should be hot but steady. Active flames burn the outer leaves before the heart becomes tender.

Eggplant Parmigiana

Palermo Caponata

Palermo-style eggplant caponata with celery, green olives, capers, tomato, and sweet-sour dressing.

title: Catania Caponata
instructions:
Catania Caponata

Catania-style caponata with eggplant, peppers, celery, olives, capers, pine nuts, and sweet-sour dressing.

2 large eggplants, about 1 1/2 lb
1 red bell pepper
1 yellow bell pepper

1 garlic clove
3 celery stalks, cut into pieces
1/3 cup pitted black olives

1/4 cup pine nuts
2 tbsp white-wine vinegar
3 tsp sugar
10 basil leaves

3 cups plus 3 tbsp peanut oil for frying
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Cut the eggplant into chunks.

2. Heat the peanut oil to 350°F.

3. Fry the eggplant until golden and drain.

4. Cut the peppers into pieces.

5. Fry them in the same oil and drain.

6. Heat 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil in a large pan.

7. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.

8. Add the basil and peeled tomatoes.

9. Cook over moderate heat for 20 minutes.

10. Blanch the celery for 5 minutes.

11. In a small pan, combine the celery, olives, capers, pine nuts, and 1 tablespoon vinegar.

12. Cook for 10 minutes.

13. Combine the tomato sauce, eggplant, peppers, and celery mixture.

14. Dissolve the sugar in the remaining vinegar.

15. Pour it into the pan.

16. Add the remaining extra-virgin olive oil and salt.

17. Stir for 2–3 minutes.

Service

Cool completely and serve cold or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Frying the eggplant and peppers separately respects their different cooking times.

title: Sicilian Peperonata
instructions:
Sicilian Peperonata

Sicilian stewed peppers with tomato, onion, garlic, basil, and a final splash of vinegar.

Yield: 4 servings

2 ripe tomatoes, cut into pieces
1 large onion, sliced
1 garlic clove
4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp white-wine vinegar
1/4 cup water or vegetable broth
10 basil leaves
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Clean the peppers, removing the stems, seeds, and membranes.

2. Cut into even pieces.

3. Heat the olive oil in a large pan.

4. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.

5. Add the peppers.

6. Cook over high heat for 4 minutes.

7. Add the tomatoes, salt, and pepper.

8. Cover and cook for 35–40 minutes, stirring every 8–10 minutes.

9. If the pan becomes too dry, add the water or broth in 2-tablespoon portions.

10. At the end, add the basil and vinegar.

11. Raise the heat and cook for 1 minute.

Service

Rest for at least 30 minutes and serve hot, warm, or cold.

Chef's note

The final rest lets the vinegar and pepper juices come together without sacrificing the vegetables' texture.

title: Melanzane Ammuttunate
instructions:
Melanzane Ammuttunate

Small Palermo-style eggplants stuffed with garlic, caciocavallo, and mint, browned and finished in tomato sauce.

1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Wash the eggplants and remove the stems.

2. Make three deep vertical cuts around each eggplant without cutting all the way through.

3. Insert garlic, caciocavallo, a mint leaf, and a small amount of salt and pepper into each cut.

4. Heat 4 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet.

5. Brown the eggplants on all sides for 8–10 minutes.

6. Heat the remaining olive oil in a separate saucepan.

7. Add the passata and cook for 10 minutes.

8. Transfer the browned eggplants to the sauce.

9. Cover partially.

10. Cook for another 10–15 minutes, turning carefully once.

11. Adjust with the remaining salt and pepper.

Service

The cuts should be deep enough to hold the filling but must not pass completely through the eggplant.

title: Carciofi alla Villanella
instructions:
Carciofi alla Villanella

Sicilian stuffed artichokes with anchovies, garlic, parsley, breadcrumbs, and Pecorino, braised with potatoes.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

8 artichokes
2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges

2 garlic cloves
1 bunch parsley, finely chopped
1/2 cup breadcrumbs
2 tbsp finely grated Pecorino or caciocavallo
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 cup water
1 lemon
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Fill a bowl with cold water and lemon juice.

2. Trim the artichokes, removing tough leaves, tips, and choke.

3. Trim the stems so the artichokes can stand upright.

4. Put them in the acidulated water.

5. Finely chop the parsley and garlic.

6. Add the chopped anchovies, breadcrumbs, cheese, salt, pepper, and 3 tablespoons olive oil.

7. Mix until moist but compact.

8. Drain and dry the artichokes.

9. Pack the filling between the leaves.

10. Stand them upright in a wide pan, placing the potatoes between them.

11. Add the water and remaining olive oil.

12. Cover.

13. Cook over low heat for 35–40 minutes, until the artichokes and potatoes are tender.

Service

Serve hot or warm with the cooking juices.

Chef's note

Packing the artichokes closely together keeps them upright so the filling stays inside during braising.

Palermo Frittella

5. Heat the olive oil in a wide pan.

6. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.

7. Drain the artichokes and add them with the fava beans and peas.

8. Add the water.

9. Season with salt and pepper.

10. Cover and cook over moderate heat for about 20 minutes, stirring gently.

11. Dissolve the sugar in the vinegar.

12. Pour it into the pan.

Chef's note

Stir gently so the fava beans and peas remain intact as they become tender.

instructions:
Broccoli Affogati

Sicilian broccoli slowly braised with onion, black olives, anchovies, Pecorino, and red wine.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb Sicilian broccoli
1 large onion, sliced
2/3 cup pitted black olives, chopped
5 oil-packed anchovy fillets
1/2 cup diced peppered Pecorino
1 cup red wine
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Clean the broccoli, separating the leaves and florets from the toughest stems.

2. Divide the florets into small clusters.

3. Wash thoroughly without drying completely.

4. Coat the bottom of a pot with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

5. Arrange one layer of broccoli.

6. Add some of the onion, olives, anchovies, and Pecorino.

7. Add a small amount of salt.

8. Repeat the layers until all ingredients are used.

9. Pour the red wine and remaining olive oil over the top.

10. Cover with a tight-fitting lid.

11. Cook over very low heat for about 90 minutes.

12. Check every 20 minutes without vigorous stirring; shake the pot gently to distribute the liquid.

13. At the end, the broccoli should be very tender but still moist.

Service

Serve hot or warm with the cooking juices.

Chef's note

The name “affogati” refers to the slow cooking in wine and the broccoli's own juices. The pan should not cook completely dry.

Cavolfiore Affogato

5. Add some of the onion, anchovies, olives, and Pecorino.

title: Sweet-and-sour Pumpkin
instructions:
Sweet-and-sour Pumpkin

Sicilian fried pumpkin with garlic, vinegar, sugar, and mint, rested overnight.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1/4 cup red-wine vinegar
2 tsp granulated sugar
2 unpeeled garlic cloves
15 fresh mint leaves
1 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds, optional

Preparation

1. Cut the pumpkin into even slices about 5/16 inch thick.

2. Heat the olive oil in a wide pan.

3. Add the unpeeled garlic cloves.

4. Cook over low heat until golden, then remove them.

5. Fry the pumpkin in batches over medium-high heat.

6. Turn once and season lightly with salt on both sides.

7. Cook until golden but still intact.

8. Transfer the pumpkin to a serving platter.

9. Dissolve the sugar in the vinegar.

10. Pour the mixture into the cooking pan.

11. Cook for 1–2 minutes while scraping the pan.

12. Pour the sweet-sour dressing over the pumpkin.

13. Add the torn mint.

14. Cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours.

Service

Let stand at room temperature for 20 minutes and finish with pumpkin seeds if using.

Chef's note

Brown the pumpkin without letting it collapse. The long rest lets the sweet-sour dressing penetrate the slices.

Sicilian Gratinated Fennel

Baked fennel with cherry tomatoes, olives, capers, Pecorino, anchovies, and breadcrumbs.

3. Cut into moderately thin slices.

4. Put the fennel, tomatoes, olives, capers, Pecorino, and about 1/3 cup breadcrumbs in a bowl.

5. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil.

6. Toss gently.

7. Transfer to a parchment-lined baking pan.

8. Season with salt and pepper.

9. Scatter the anchovy pieces over the top.

10. Sprinkle with the remaining breadcrumbs.

11. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

12. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until the fennel is tender and the top golden.

Slice the fennel evenly so the topping browns in the same time the interior becomes tender.

Peperoni Ammollicati

Sicilian peppers with toasted breadcrumbs, olives, Pecorino, pine nuts, capers, garlic, and oregano.

3. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a nonstick skillet with 1 garlic clove.

4. Add the breadcrumbs and toast over high heat, stirring continuously.

5. Reserve.

6. Clean the peppers and cut into strips.

7. Heat the remaining 4 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet.

8. Add the remaining 3 garlic cloves and cook for 1 minute.

9. Add the peppers.

10. Sauté briefly over high heat.

11. Add the salt.

12. Cover and cook for about 20 minutes.

13. Add the olives, capers, and pine nuts.

14. Continue cooking for another 15 minutes.

15. Cool slightly.

16. Add the Pecorino, toasted breadcrumbs, and oregano.

title: Lampascioni in Olive Oil
instructions:
Lampascioni in Olive Oil

Puglian lampascioni bulbs boiled in water and vinegar, flavored with garlic, bay, chile, and oregano, then packed in olive oil.

Yield: 6 jars

2 tbsp coarse salt
2 garlic cloves, sliced
2 bay leaves, torn
1 small piece dried chile
2 tsp dried oregano
5 cups extra-virgin olive oil for covering

Preparation

1. Remove the tough outer layer from the lampascioni.

2. Score the base lightly.

3. Soak in cold water for 4 hours, changing the water every hour.

4. Bring the water, vinegar, and salt to a boil.

5. Add the lampascioni.

6. Cook for 30–40 minutes, until tender but intact.

7. Drain.

8. Spread on a clean kitchen towel.

9. Dry completely for at least 1 hour.

10. Sterilize 6 jars.

11. Fill them with alternating lampascioni, garlic, bay, chile, and oregano.

12. Pour in olive oil until completely covered.

13. Remove air bubbles with a clean skewer.

14. Check after 1 hour that the lampascioni remain completely submerged and add more oil if needed.

Service

Chef's note

The lampascioni must be completely dry before packing in oil and must remain fully submerged during storage.

Sweet-and-sour Lampascioni

Puglian lampascioni bulbs boiled and then glazed with vinegar, sugar, garlic, bay, and black pepper.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 tbsp plus 1 tsp sugar

Preparation

1. Remove the rootlets and tough outer layers.

2. Wash the lampascioni thoroughly.

3. Score the base lightly in a cross.

4. Bring the water to a boil with about 1/2 teaspoon salt.

5. Boil the lampascioni for about 20 minutes, until tender but intact.

6. Drain well.

8. Add the garlic and bay leaves and cook for 1 minute.

10. Sauté for 3–4 minutes.

11. Pour in the vinegar.

12. Add the sugar and peppercorns.

13. Cook for 5–7 minutes, until the liquid reduces slightly.

14. Add the remaining salt.

15. Remove from the heat and cool in the dressing.

Service

Puglian Stuffed Eggplants

Baked eggplants filled with cherry tomatoes, capers, eggs, Pecorino, breadcrumbs, oregano, and parsley.

Browning the shells and filling separately prevents a watery stuffing and helps the eggplant keep its structure.

Stewed Broccoli Rabe

2. Wash thoroughly in several changes of cold water.

3. Transfer it to a large pot while still wet, without adding extra water.

4. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes.

5. Drain away the bitter liquid released in the pot.

6. Add the garlic, bay leaves, olive oil, salt, and pepper.

7. Pour in the rosé wine.

8. Cover again.

9. Cook over low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring gently every 5 minutes.

Chef's note

Draining the liquid released during the first stage reduces bitterness without washing away the flavor of the greens.

instructions:
Fava Bean Purée with Chicory

Puglian dried-fava purée served with boiled chicory and extra-virgin olive oil.

Ingredients

Preparation

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Put the fava beans in a pot with the measured fresh water.

4. Bring to a gentle boil.

5. Skim as needed.

6. Cook over low heat for about 1 hour, until the beans break down easily.

7. Add about 2/3 teaspoon salt.

8. Blend or stir vigorously with 2 tablespoons olive oil until smooth and thick.

9. Trim the chicory, removing tough portions.

10. Bring the cooking water to a boil with the remaining salt.

11. Boil the chicory for 12–15 minutes.

12. Drain and squeeze well.

Service

Spoon the fava purée onto plates, add the chicory, and finish with the remaining olive oil and toasted bread.

Chef's note

Keep the purée fairly thick. It firms further as it cools, so do not evaporate too much liquid during cooking.

Puglian Stuffed Artichokes

4. Coarsely process the bread with the parsley.

5. Transfer to a bowl.

6. Add the garlic, Pecorino, eggs, salt, and pepper.

9. Open the centers gently and pack in the filling.

10. Arrange the artichokes snugly in a high-sided skillet.

11. Add the olive oil, wine, and water until the liquid reaches roughly two-thirds of their height.

12. Cover.

13. Cook over medium-low heat for 20–25 minutes.

Potato, Rice, and Mussel Tiella

Bari-style baked layers of potatoes, rice, mussels, tomatoes, onion, garlic, parsley, and cheese.

Yield: 6 servings

2 1/4 lb fresh mussels, cleaned
about 3 1/3 cups thinly sliced potatoes
1 cup Carnaroli rice

1 onion, thinly sliced
2 garlic cloves, minced
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley

1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 cup dry white wine
1 1/4 cups water, plus strained mussel liquid
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Clean the mussels thoroughly.

2. Open them in a covered saucepan with 2 tablespoons olive oil for 1–2 minutes, or open them raw by hand.

3. Remove the empty half-shell from each mussel.

4. Strain the mussel liquid very carefully.

5. Mix it with the measured water.

6. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

7. Grease a baking dish with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

8. Arrange half of the potatoes, tomatoes, onion, garlic, and parsley.

9. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

10. Add half of the grated cheeses.

11. Arrange half of the mussels meat-side up.

12. Scatter half of the uncooked rice over them.

13. Repeat the layers.

14. Pour the wine around the edges.

15. Add the diluted mussel liquid until it nearly reaches the top layer.

16. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

17. Cover with a lid or foil.

18. Bake for 45–50 minutes.

19. Uncover and continue for another 15 minutes.

20. Check that the rice is cooked and nearly all of the liquid has been absorbed.

Service

Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

Chef's note

Pouring the liquid around the edges keeps the layers in place and prevents the grated cheese from being washed off the surface.

5. Add more water gradually only until the bread softens without becoming mushy.

4. When the oil is hot but not smoking, add only 1–2 peppers at a time.

7. Drain immediately on paper towels.

8. Cool completely.

9. Season with salt after cooling.

The peppers become crisp as they cool. Frying too long darkens them and creates bitterness.

3. Scoop out the flesh, leaving shells about 3/8 inch thick.

4. Dice the removed flesh.

5. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet with 1 garlic clove.

6. Add the eggplant flesh and cook until golden, about 8–10 minutes.

7. Drain on paper towels.

8. Brown the ground veal in the same skillet for 4–5 minutes.

9. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil with the remaining garlic in a second skillet.

10. Add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes.

11. Add the basil and half of the salt.

12. In a bowl, combine the cooked eggplant, veal, eggs, bread, Parmigiano, parsley, pepper, and remaining salt.

13. Mix thoroughly.

14. Put several cubes of scamorza in the bottom of each eggplant shell.

15. Fill with the mixture.

16. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet.

17. Brown the stuffed eggplants filling-side down for 2–3 minutes.

18. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

19. Arrange the eggplants in a baking dish.

20. Spoon the tomato sauce over them.

21. Add the oregano and remaining olive oil.

title: Potatoes with Crispy Senise Peppers
instructions:
Potatoes with Crispy Senise Peppers

Lucanian potatoes sautéed with dried Senise peppers flash-fried until crisp.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 3/4 lb potatoes
about 3 cups whole dried Senise peppers
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a boil.

2. Boil the whole potatoes for 10 minutes.

3. Drain, cool slightly, and peel.

4. Cut the potatoes into slices about 3/16 inch thick.

5. Clean the dried peppers with a dry cloth.

6. Remove the stems and seeds.

7. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet.

8. Fry the peppers for only a few seconds, one or two at a time, until puffed and bright red.

9. Drain immediately on paper towels and cool.

10. Add the remaining olive oil to the same skillet.

11. Add the potatoes and cook over medium-high heat for 10–12 minutes, turning gently until well browned.

12. Add the salt.

13. Break the crisp peppers into coarse pieces.

14. Add them to the potatoes.

15. Toss together for 1–2 minutes.

Service

Chef's note

The peppers become crisp as they cool. Frying them too long makes them dark and bitter.

title: Calabrian Stuffed Eggplants
instructions:
Calabrian Stuffed Eggplants

Calabrian eggplants filled with their own flesh, stale bread, Pecorino, eggs, tomato paste, and parsley.

Yield: 4 servings

4 medium eggplants
about 3 cups fresh stale breadcrumbs

1 cup finely grated Pecorino

2 garlic cloves, minced
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
10 basil leaves
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil

1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Cut the eggplants in half lengthwise.

2. Scoop out the flesh, keeping the shells intact.

3. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil with the vinegar.

4. Cook the shells for about 15–20 minutes.

5. Drain and dry upside down.

6. Chop the removed eggplant flesh.

7. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet.

8. Add the garlic and eggplant flesh.

9. Cook for 20–25 minutes, until tender and fairly dry.

10. Cool slightly.

11. Mix the cooked eggplant, stale bread, eggs, Pecorino, tomato paste, parsley, and the main portion of breadcrumbs.

12. Add the salt.

13. Fill the eggplant shells.

14. Preheat the oven to 480°F.

15. Arrange the eggplants in a baking pan.

16. Sprinkle with the remaining breadcrumbs.

17. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

18. Bake for 15–18 minutes, until deeply golden on top.

Service

Finish with fresh basil and serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

The filling should be fairly dry before it goes into the shells. Wet eggplant flesh makes the finished dish soft and difficult to portion.

title: Calabrian Zucchini
instructions:
Calabrian Zucchini

Calabrian zucchini marinated with garlic, fresh red pepper, mint, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
1 cup plus 1 tbsp white-wine vinegar
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 garlic cloves, sliced
1/2 red bell pepper, finely chopped
15 fresh mint leaves
2 tsp fine salt, divided

Preparation

1. Wash the zucchini.

2. Trim the ends.

3. Cut in half lengthwise.

4. Remove the seedy center.

5. Cut into thin slices.

6. Layer the zucchini in a bowl, sprinkling each layer with some of the salt.

7. Rest for 4 hours.

8. Squeeze very thoroughly.

9. Bring the water, vinegar, and about 2/3 teaspoon salt to a boil.

10. Blanch the zucchini for 2 minutes.

11. Drain.

12. Spread on a clean towel and cool and dry completely.

13. Press again to remove as much water as possible.

14. Dress with the red pepper, garlic, mint, and olive oil.

Service

Rest for at least 1 hour before serving.

Chef's note

Removing as much water as possible before dressing keeps the zucchini firm and helps the oil and aromatics cling to it.

Vruocculi Affucati

1 pinch dried chile
1/2 cup red or white wine

1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley

Preparation

1. Clean the cauliflower.

2. Divide it into even florets.

3. Heat the olive oil in a wide saucepan.

4. Add the garlic, chile, and anchovies.

5. Cook for 1–2 minutes, until the anchovies dissolve.

6. Add the cauliflower.

7. Sauté for 3 minutes.

8. Pour in the wine.

9. Add the olives.

10. Season with salt and pepper.

11. Cover.

12. Cook over low heat for 25–30 minutes, stirring gently every 8 minutes.

13. Uncover for the final 5 minutes if the pan juices remain abundant.

Service

Finish with parsley and some of the cooking juices.

Chef's note

The covered cooking “drowns” the cauliflower in its own steam and wine without requiring added water.

instructions:
Fagioli alla Pignata

Calabrian cannellini beans slowly cooked in earthenware with tomato, celery, garlic, basil, oregano, and chile.

10 basil leaves
1 tsp dried oregano
2 fresh chiles
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
2 2/3 qt water

Preparation

1. Soak the beans in cold water for 12 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Put the beans in an earthenware pot.

4. Cover with the measured water.

5. Bring very slowly to a simmer.

6. Cook for about 60–90 minutes, until nearly tender.

7. Boil the celery separately for 10 minutes.

8. Chop the celery.

9. Peel and chop the tomatoes.

10. Combine the celery, tomatoes, parsley, 1 garlic clove, and basil.

11. Pour this mixture over the beans without stirring aggressively.

12. Cook over very low heat for about 1 hour.

13. Ten minutes before the end, add the olive oil, oregano, whole chiles, remaining garlic, and salt.

Service

Serve with toasted bread.

Chef's note

Very slow cooking in earthenware creates a creamy broth without excessively breaking the beans.

5. Arrange the onions cut-side up.

9. Spread the breadcrumb mixture over the onions.

10. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

11. Return to the oven.

12. Bake for 30–40 minutes, until the onions are tender and the topping deeply golden.

The first short bake softens the onions before the topping is added, preventing the breadcrumbs from burning before the centers become tender.

Potato Frico

Friulian crisp potato cake with onion and Montasio cheese.

Ingredients

about 5 cups coarsely grated Montasio
1/2 onion, thinly sliced
2 tbsp oil
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Put the potatoes in a pot and cover with cold water.

2. Bring to a boil.

3. Cook until fork-tender.

4. Drain, cool slightly, and peel.

5. Mash the potatoes.

6. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet.

7. Add the onion and cook until golden.

8. Add the potatoes.

9. Season with salt and pepper.

10. Add the Montasio.

11. Stir over medium heat until the cheese is completely melted and evenly distributed.

12. Grease a nonstick skillet with the remaining oil.

13. Transfer the mixture and flatten it into a layer about 3/4–1 1/4 inches thick.

14. Cook over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, until a deep golden crust forms underneath.

15. Turn the frico with the help of a plate.

16. Cook the second side for another 8–10 minutes.

Rest for 5 minutes and cut into wedges.

Chef's note

Wait until a firm crust has formed before turning the frico so it stays intact and crisp.

Patate in Tecia

Friulian skillet potatoes mashed coarsely with onion, lard or pancetta, and broth, then browned on the bottom.

5. Put the lard and onion in a heavy skillet.

13. Cook over very low heat for 30–40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.

14. Uncover during the final minutes and let the liquid evaporate completely.

Chef's note

Toasting the flour in the lard naturally binds the sauerkraut and thickens its cooking liquid during the second stage.

5. Cook over low heat for 8 minutes.

14. Continue until the brovada turns chestnut-brown and becomes very tender.

15. Adjust the salt and pepper only at the end.

Service

Chef's note

The long cooking rounds out the acidity of the fermented turnips. Add broth gradually instead of flooding the pot.

instructions:
Radicchio with Cracklings

Friulian radicchio dressed with vinegar and olive oil, then topped with hot crisp pork cracklings.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 heads radicchio
about 3/4 cup pork cracklings
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp red-wine vinegar
1/2 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Trim the radicchio and discard damaged leaves.

2. Wash and dry it completely.

3. Tear into pieces and transfer to a bowl.

4. Dress with 1 tablespoon olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper.

5. Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet.

6. Add the cracklings.

7. Cook for about 5 minutes, until very hot and crisp.

8. Immediately pour the cracklings and hot oil over the radicchio.

9. Toss quickly.

Service

Serve immediately, while the radicchio is still fresh but lightly wilted by the hot fat.

Chef's note

The contrast between cool radicchio and sizzling cracklings defines the dish, so add the hot topping only at the last moment.

title: Soft Frico
instructions:
Soft Frico

Friulian soft frico made with potatoes, onion, and Montasio, browned on both sides.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/3 lb potatoes
about 3 cups diced Montasio in mixed ages
1 small white or yellow onion, thinly sliced
2 tbsp oil
1 cup water, divided
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a nonstick skillet.

2. Add the onion.

3. Add 1/4 cup water.

4. Cook gently for 5–6 minutes.

5. Peel the potatoes and slice them very thin.

6. Add them to the onion.

7. Add 1/2 cup water.

8. Cover partially.

9. Cook slowly for about 40 minutes, stirring gently and adding the remaining water only if needed.

10. Coarsely mash some of the potatoes with a spoon.

11. Add the Montasio.

12. Stir until completely melted.

13. Add the salt.

14. Press the mixture into an even cake in the skillet.

15. Cook without stirring until the bottom is golden.

16. Turn with the help of a plate.

17. Cook the second side until crisp and browned.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and cut into wedges.

Chef's note

The center should remain soft and stretchy while only the outer surfaces become crisp.

title: Crispy Frico
instructions:
Crispy Frico

Thin crisp Friulian wafers made from aged Montasio cheese.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 3 cups finely grated 16–18-month Montasio
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. Finely grate the Montasio.

2. Lightly grease a nonstick skillet about 6 inches wide with a very small amount of the olive oil.

3. Heat over medium-high heat.

4. Scatter about one-quarter of the cheese in a thin even layer.

5. Cook until melted and golden underneath, about 2–3 minutes.

6. Turn with a wide spatula.

7. Cook the second side for 1–2 minutes.

8. Transfer to parchment or a wire rack.

9. Repeat with the remaining cheese.

Service

Serve flat as a crisp wafer or shape while still hot over an inverted bowl to make a basket.

Chef's note

Crispy frico should be very thin. A thick layer retains more fat and stays soft in the center.

title: Capuzi Garbi
instructions:
Capuzi Garbi

Trieste-style fermented cabbage cooked with onion, flour, lard, and caraway until dry and richly flavored.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb fermented sauerkraut
1 onion, finely chopped
2 tbsp flour
2 tbsp lard
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
1 tsp caraway seeds
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Put the fermented cabbage in a saucepan.

2. Add enough water to come almost level with it.

3. Cook for about 30 minutes.

4. Meanwhile, melt the lard in a second saucepan.

5. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.

6. Add the flour.

7. Stir until lightly golden.

8. Add the cabbage and its cooking water.

9. Add the salt, pepper, and caraway.

10. Cover.

11. Cook over very low heat for 30–40 minutes.

12. Stir every 10 minutes.

13. Uncover and continue until all of the liquid has been absorbed.

Service

Serve very hot.

Chef's note

The second long cooking concentrates the cabbage's acidity and lets the toasted flour bind the liquid.

title: Grilled Treviso Radicchio
instructions:
Grilled Treviso Radicchio

Late-season Treviso radicchio grilled and finished with extra-virgin olive oil, salt, and optional balsamic vinegar.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 heads late-season Treviso radicchio
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp balsamic vinegar, optional

Preparation

1. Rinse the heads quickly and dry thoroughly.

2. Cut them in half lengthwise, keeping the core intact so the leaves stay together.

3. Brush the cut sides with 2 tablespoons olive oil.

4. Heat a grill or grill pan over high heat.

5. Place the radicchio cut-side down.

6. Grill for 3–4 minutes.

7. Turn.

8. Cook for another 2–3 minutes, until the leaves are tender and the edges lightly charred.

9. Season with salt and the remaining olive oil.

Service

Finish with balsamic vinegar if using and serve immediately.

Chef's note

The grill should be very hot so the radicchio roasts quickly instead of steaming and becoming watery.

title: Venetian Peperonata
instructions:
Venetian Peperonata

Venetian stewed peppers with tomatoes, zucchini, onion, garlic, butter, and olive oil.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

about 1 lb mixed bell peppers
2 2/3 cups plum tomatoes
1 medium zucchini
1 yellow onion
2 garlic cloves
4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp butter
8 basil leaves, optional
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Finely chop the onion.

2. Clean the peppers, removing the stems, seeds, and ribs.

3. Cut into even pieces.

4. Cut the zucchini into batons.

5. Score the tomatoes.

6. Blanch them in boiling water for 30 seconds.

7. Chill in ice water.

8. Peel, seed, and chop the tomato flesh.

9. Mince the garlic.

10. Heat the olive oil and butter in a saucepan.

11. Add the onion, garlic, and half of the salt.

12. Cook over low heat for 5–6 minutes.

13. Add the peppers.

14. Sauté for 2 minutes.

15. Add the tomatoes.

16. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.

17. Uncover.

18. Add the zucchini.

19. Season with the remaining salt and pepper.

20. Cook for another 10 minutes.

Service

Finish with basil if using and serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

Add the zucchini only during the final 10 minutes so it stays distinct instead of collapsing into the pepper sauce.

title: Venetian Beans with Salsa
instructions:
Venetian Beans with Salsa

Venetian beans served with a long-cooked sauce of soppressa, anchovies, onion, parsley, olive oil, and vinegar.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

about 6 cups cooked Lamon or borlotti beans
about 1 1/2 cups finely chopped soppressa
about 2/3 cup finely chopped anchovy fillets
1 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
about 1 3/4 cups finely chopped onions
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp white-wine vinegar

Preparation

1. If using dried beans, soak them for 12 hours and boil until tender.

2. Finely chop the soppressa, anchovies, parsley, and onions.

3. Put everything in a heavy saucepan with the olive oil.

4. Set over the lowest heat.

5. Cook for about 2 hours, stirring gently every 10–15 minutes.

6. Make sure the sauce does not catch or become too dark.

7. Turn off the heat.

8. Add the vinegar gradually while stirring.

9. Warm the beans separately if necessary.

Service

Divide the beans among plates and add about 3 tablespoons sauce to each serving.

Chef's note

Cook the sauce very slowly. High heat burns the onion and anchovies before the soppressa has time to render and meld into the sauce.

Funghi in Tecia

Venetian skillet mushrooms with dried porcini, garlic, parsley, olive oil, salt, and pepper.

about 3 cups sliced oyster mushrooms
about 1 cup loosely packed dried porcini

4 garlic cloves
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Soak the dried porcini in warm water for 10 minutes.

2. Lift them out by hand.

3. Rinse again in clean water and drain.

4. Chop coarsely.

5. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet.

6. Add the garlic and let it color lightly.

7. Remove the garlic.

8. Add the fresh mushrooms and porcini.

9. Cook uncovered for about 10 minutes, stirring regularly.

10. Season with salt and pepper.

11. Add the parsley during the final minute.

Service

Serve immediately while hot.

Chef's note

Cooking uncovered lets the mushrooms release and evaporate their water instead of steaming in it.

Venetian-style Potatoes

Venetian potatoes browned with butter, olive oil, onion, and parsley.

2 lb potatoes

1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 onion, thinly sliced
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1 1/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Wash and peel the potatoes.

2. Cut into even pieces about 1 1/4 inches wide.

3. Melt the butter with the olive oil in a wide skillet.

4. Add the onion.

5. Cook for 5–6 minutes, until soft but not dark.

6. Add the potatoes.

7. Cook over medium heat for about 30 minutes.

8. Turn often but gently so several sides brown without breaking.

9. Add the salt only during the final 5 minutes.

10. Turn off the heat.

11. Add the parsley.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Salting near the end limits moisture release and helps the potatoes develop a better browned surface.

title: Venetian Stuffed Artichokes

Venetian Stuffed Artichokes

Venetian artichokes stuffed with breadcrumbs, garlic, and mint, then braised upside down in olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

6 artichokes
6 tbsp breadcrumbs
1 garlic clove, minced
6 mint leaves, finely chopped
1 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Trim the artichokes, removing tough outer leaves, tips, and stems.

2. Gently open the center of each artichoke.

3. Mix the breadcrumbs, garlic, mint, and half of the salt.

4. Fill the artichokes with the mixture.

5. Arrange them upside down in a snug saucepan.

6. Pour in the olive oil.

7. Add water to reach halfway up the artichokes.

8. Add the remaining salt.

9. Cover.

10. Cook over medium heat for 20–30 minutes, until the hearts are tender.

11. Uncover during the final minutes and let nearly all of the liquid evaporate.

Service

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

Keeping the artichokes upside down and tightly packed helps the filling remain inside during braising.

instructions:
Green Beans with Tomato

Venetian-style green beans slowly cooked with tomato, garlic, olive oil, and optional basil.

1 1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Trim the ends from the green beans.

2. Wash thoroughly.

3. Heat the olive oil in a wide saucepan.

4. Add the garlic.

5. After 30 seconds, add the green beans.

6. Toss to coat with the oil.

7. Add the tomato passata or crushed tomatoes.

8. Add the water.

9. Season with salt.

10. Cover and bring to a gentle simmer.

11. Cook over medium-low heat for about 30 minutes.

12. Remove the lid.

13. Continue for another 10 minutes, until the beans are tender but not collapsing.

14. Add the basil during the final 2 minutes if using.

Service

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

The beans should cook long enough in the tomato to absorb its flavor while still retaining a slight bite.

title: Verze Sofegae
instructions:
Verze Sofegae

Venetian cabbage slowly stewed with onion, garlic, goose fat, olive oil, vinegar, and broth.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb Savoy cabbage, cut into strips
1 onion, sliced
2 garlic cloves, crushed
about 3/4 cup goose fat
4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp vinegar
4 1/4 cups hot vegetable broth
1 1/4 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Wash the cabbage and cut it into strips.

2. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan.

3. Add the goose fat.

4. Cook until it begins to render.

5. Add the garlic and onion.

6. Cook for 6–8 minutes.

7. Add the cabbage.

8. Stir until it begins to wilt.

9. Add 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons broth.

10. Season with salt and pepper.

11. Cover and cook over very low heat for about 90 minutes.

12. Stir every 15 minutes.

13. Add more broth in 1/2-cup portions as needed.

14. During the final 10 minutes, add the vinegar.

15. Uncover if needed to reduce the cooking liquid.

Service

Serve very hot.

Chef's note

Long gentle cooking turns the cabbage soft and concentrated. Add the broth gradually rather than all at once.

6. Season with salt and pepper.

7. Cook over low heat for 10–15 minutes.

title: Pearà
instructions:
Pearà

Verona bread sauce with beef marrow, meat broth, butter, and abundant black pepper, cooked very slowly.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

about 10 cups coarse stale breadcrumbs
3 1/3 cups boiling beef broth
about 1 1/2 cups beef marrow
3 1/2 tbsp butter
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
2 tsp black pepper, one-third finely ground and the rest coarsely ground

Preparation

1. Cut the bread and dry it in a 265°F oven until crisp but still pale.

2. Cool completely.

3. Grate or process into coarse crumbs.

4. Put the marrow and butter in an earthenware or heavy pot.

5. Melt over very low heat.

6. Add the breadcrumbs.

7. Stir for 2 minutes.

8. Gradually whisk in the boiling broth.

9. Cover partially.

10. Cook at the gentlest simmer for 90 minutes, stirring periodically.

11. Add the pepper and salt.

12. Cook for another 10 minutes.

13. If the sauce is too thick, add 1/4–1/2 cup hot broth; if too loose, cook uncovered for several minutes.

14. Turn off the heat and add the olive oil.

Service

Serve piping hot with mixed boiled meats.

Chef's note

Pearà should barely simmer. A hard boil makes the sauce heavy and increases the risk of scorching.

4. Heat a grill or griddle very thoroughly.

5. Lightly brush the slices with olive oil or melted butter.

6. Arrange the slices on the hot surface without overlapping.

8. Turn once they release easily and show deep grill marks.

9. Cook the second side for another 4–5 minutes.

A very hot cooking surface creates the crust quickly and prevents the polenta from sticking or drying out inside.

Lombardy-style cabbage stewed with sausage, onion, garlic, white wine, broth, and bay.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb Savoy cabbage, cut into strips
1 1/8 lb Italian sausage, casings removed
1 medium onion, finely chopped
2 garlic cloves, minced
2 tbsp olive oil
1/2 cup dry white wine
1 cup hot chicken or vegetable broth, plus 1/2 cup available if needed
1 bay leaf
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 pinch red-pepper flakes, optional

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan.

2. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.

3. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

4. Add the crumbled sausage.

5. Brown for 7–8 minutes, breaking it apart with a spoon.

6. Remove any excessive rendered fat.

7. Pour in the white wine and scrape the bottom of the pan.

8. Cook for 2–3 minutes, until the wine is nearly evaporated.

9. Add the cabbage, bay leaf, salt, pepper, and optional red-pepper flakes.

10. Pour in 1 cup broth.

11. Bring to a gentle simmer.

12. Cover and cook over low heat for about 60 minutes, stirring every 10–15 minutes.

13. Add more broth in small amounts only if the pan becomes too dry.

14. Remove the bay leaf.

Service

Serve very hot with rustic bread.

Chef's note

Cook the cabbage slowly until soft and sweet while the sausage seasons the braising liquid without overwhelming it.

title: Potatoes Savoy Style
instructions:
Potatoes Savoy Style

Yellow potatoes baked with milk, butter, provola, and nutmeg, then gratinated until golden.

Yield: 4–6 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb yellow potatoes
about 2 cups thinly sliced provola
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp whole milk
7 tbsp butter, divided
1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 375°F.

2. Wash the potatoes very thoroughly without peeling them.

3. Dry and cut into even slices about 1/8 inch thick, keeping each potato roughly reassembled.

4. Pour the milk into a baking dish.

5. Add half of the salt, the pepper, and nutmeg.

6. Arrange the potatoes in the milk, tilting them so the slices overlap.

7. Dot with about 5 tablespoons butter.

8. Add the remaining salt.

9. Bake for 20–25 minutes.

10. Remove the dish from the oven.

11. Scatter the provola over the potatoes.

12. Add the remaining butter.

13. Increase the oven to 445°F.

14. Return to the oven until the cheese is melted and deeply golden, about 8–10 minutes.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve hot.

Uniform slices allow the potatoes to cook at the same rate and absorb the milk without remaining raw in the center.

Funghi Trifolati

Porcini, chanterelles, cardoncelli, and button mushrooms sautéed with garlic, parsley, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Baked Cheesy Polenta

Lombardy-style polenta enriched with Gorgonzola, mozzarella, soft cheeses, and Parmigiano, then baked until golden.

8. Fold in the creamy cheese.

9. Cook for another 10 minutes, stirring continuously.

11. Transfer the polenta to a baking dish greased with about 2 teaspoons butter.

12. Sprinkle with Parmigiano.

13. Dot the remaining butter over the top.

Drain the mozzarella thoroughly so it does not release excessive water into the polenta while baking.

Spiced Green Beans and Cashews

Piedmont Stuffed Onions

13. Add it to the beef filling.

Gratinated Cardo Gobbo

1 3/4 lb cardoon

1/4 cup breadcrumbs
1 cup plus 2 tbsp hot meat broth
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 lemon
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

3. Fill a bowl with cold water and the juice of half the lemon.

4. Place the cardoon in the acidulated water as it is cleaned.

5. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

6. Add the remaining half lemon, sliced.

7. Boil the cardoon for about 20 minutes, until tender.

8. Drain very thoroughly.

9. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

10. Grease a baking dish with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

11. Arrange the cardoon in one or two layers.

12. Add the salt.

13. Sprinkle with the breadcrumbs and Parmigiano.

14. Pour the broth around the edges.

15. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

16. Bake for about 30 minutes, until golden on top and most of the broth is absorbed.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve hot.

Chef's note

Drain the cardoon thoroughly before baking so it does not dilute the broth and prevent the top from browning.

instructions:
Roasted Peppers with Bagna Càuda

Roasted Carmagnola peppers served with Piedmont garlic-and-anchovy bagna càuda.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 meaty red and yellow Carmagnola or bell peppers
8 garlic cloves
8 salt-packed anchovies, rinsed and deboned
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 cup plus 1 tbsp whole milk, optional for soaking the garlic
1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 400°F or prepare a very hot grill.

2. Roast the whole peppers, turning until the skins are evenly blackened.

3. Transfer immediately to a bowl and cover.

4. Rest for 10 minutes.

5. Peel the peppers.

6. Remove the seeds and membranes.

7. Cut into wide strips.

8. Remove the germ from the garlic cloves.

9. For a milder sauce, soak the garlic in the milk for 1 hour and drain.

10. Put the garlic in a small saucepan with about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon olive oil.

11. Cook over the lowest heat for about 30 minutes without frying.

12. Gradually mash the garlic with a wooden spoon.

13. Add the anchovies.

14. Stir until completely dissolved.

15. Add the remaining olive oil.

16. Cook over the lowest heat for another 20 minutes.

Service

Arrange the peppers on plates and serve with warm bagna càuda.

Chef's note

Bagna càuda should never fry. Gentle heat turns the garlic and anchovies into a creamy sauce without bitterness.

Vegetable Finanziera

2. Add the onion and garlic.

3. Cook for 5 minutes.

6. Add the artichokes.

7. Continue for another 5 minutes.

8. Add the mushrooms and peas.

9. Season with salt and pepper.

10. Pour in the broth.

11. Cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.

12. Remove the lid.

13. Continue for 5 minutes, until the liquid is nearly reduced and the vegetables are tender but still distinct.

15. Add the lemon juice.

4. Boil the stems for 5–6 minutes, until tender but still firm.

Ligurian Stuffed Zucchini

Add the breadcrumbs gradually. The filling should remain soft rather than becoming dry.

instructions:
Genoese Chard with Pine Nuts

instructions:
Fagioli All'uccelletto

Tuscan cannellini beans slowly cooked with tomato, garlic, sage, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 cups dried cannellini beans
1 1/4 cups crushed ripe or canned peeled tomatoes
4 unpeeled garlic cloves
8 sage leaves
7 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2 1/8 qt water
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Rinse the beans.

2. Put them in an earthenware pot with the cold water.

3. Add 2 garlic cloves, 4 sage leaves, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and several peppercorns.

4. Bring to the barest possible simmer.

5. Cook over very low heat for about 2 hours without vigorous bubbling.

6. Add half of the salt only once the beans are tender.

7. Let the beans cool slightly in their cooking water.

8. Heat the remaining 5 tablespoons olive oil in another earthenware pot.

9. Add the remaining garlic cloves and sage.

10. Cook for 2 minutes.

11. Add the tomatoes.

12. Season with the remaining salt and pepper.

13. Cook for about 20 minutes.

14. Drain the beans gently, reserving 1/2 cup cooking liquid.

15. Add the beans to the sauce.

16. Cook for another 15 minutes, stirring gently.

17. Add a little reserved bean liquid only if the sauce becomes too dry.

Service

Serve very hot with Tuscan-style bread.

Chef's note

Cooking the cannellini at a barely perceptible simmer keeps them intact before they enter the tomato sauce.

Tuscan Skillet-roasted Potatoes

Tuscan potatoes cooked very slowly in a skillet with olive oil, sage, salt, and pepper until deeply golden.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb potatoes
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
8 sage leaves
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Peel the potatoes.

2. Cut them in half or into very thick even slices.

3. Pour the olive oil into a wide skillet to form a thin layer over the bottom.

4. Arrange the potatoes in a single layer.

5. Season the exposed surfaces with half of the salt and pepper.

6. Place the sage leaves between the potatoes.

7. Start over high heat.

8. As soon as the oil begins to sizzle, reduce the heat to the lowest setting.

9. Cover.

10. Cook very slowly for 3–3 1/2 hours.

11. Turn the potatoes about every 30 minutes.

12. With each turn, distribute the remaining salt and pepper over newly exposed surfaces.

13. Uncover for the final 10 minutes to dry and crisp the crust.

Serve immediately.

The long low-heat cooking creates a creamy interior and deeply browned crust without scorching the oil.

instructions:
Gobbi Rifatti

Tuscan cardoons boiled with lemon, battered and fried, then finished in tomato sauce with Pecorino.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

3 1/4 lb cardoons
4 1/4 cups crushed peeled tomatoes
1 dried chile
2 unwaxed lemons
3 garlic cloves
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus 3 cups plus 3 tbsp for frying
1 cup finely grated aged Pecorino
1 1/3 tsp fine salt

For the batter
1 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp cold sparkling water
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
4 egg whites

Preparation

1. Cut away the base of the cardoons and separate the ribs.

2. Discard tough and damaged outer ribs.

3. Remove leaves and strings.

4. Cut the ribs in half.

5. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

6. Squeeze in the lemon juice and add the peels.

7. Boil the cardoons for about 30 minutes, until tender.

8. Drain, cool, and dry very thoroughly.

9. Cut into large pieces.

10. Make the batter by mixing the flour, sparkling water, and olive oil.

11. Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks.

12. Fold them gently into the batter.

13. Heat the frying oil to 350°F.

14. Dip the cardoons into the batter.

15. Fry in small batches until golden.

16. Drain on paper towels.

17. Heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a saucepan.

18. Add the garlic and chile.

19. Remove the garlic once golden.

20. Add the tomatoes.

21. Season with salt and cook for 5 minutes.

22. Add the fried cardoons.

23. Coat with the sauce and cook for 4–5 minutes.

24. Turn off the heat.

25. Sprinkle with Pecorino.

26. Cover for 2 minutes, until the cheese softens slightly.

Service

Serve very hot.

Chef's note

Dry the cardoons thoroughly before battering to reduce splattering and help the coating adhere.

Carciofi Ritti

Empoli-style upright artichokes stuffed with pancetta, garlic, parsley, and artichoke stems, braised with white wine.

about 3/4 cup finely chopped pancetta
2 garlic cloves

2. Cut off the tips.

3. Trim the stems so the artichokes can stand upright.

4. Peel the stems.

5. Gently open the centers of the artichokes.

6. Finely chop the pancetta, parsley, garlic, and half of the stems.

7. Add half of the salt.

8. Pack the mixture into the artichoke centers.

9. Heat the olive oil in a pan narrow enough to keep the artichokes close together.

10. Stand the artichokes upright.

11. Add the remaining stems, cut into pieces.

12. Pour in the white wine.

13. Add the remaining salt.

14. Cover.

15. Cook over low heat for about 30 minutes.

16. Make sure the pan does not dry completely; add 1/4 cup hot water only if needed.

Spinach Florentine

Florentine spinach with eggs, béchamel, and Parmigiano, baked until golden.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb spinach
4 large eggs
7 tbsp butter, divided
2 cups plus 2 tbsp milk
1/4 cup flour
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano, divided
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Clean and wash the spinach.

2. Put it in a pot with only the water clinging to the leaves.

3. Cover and cook for about 10 minutes.

4. Drain, cool, and squeeze very dry.

5. Chop coarsely.

6. Melt about 3 1/2 tablespoons butter in a skillet.

7. Add the spinach and about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

8. Cook for 3–4 minutes.

9. For the béchamel, melt about 3 tablespoons butter in a saucepan.

10. Add the flour.

11. Stir for 1 minute.

12. Gradually whisk in the hot milk.

13. Cook, stirring, until thickened, about 5–7 minutes.

14. Add half of the Parmigiano, salt, and pepper.

15. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

16. Butter a baking dish with the remaining butter.

17. Spread in the spinach.

18. Make four wells.

19. Crack one egg into each well.

20. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

21. Cover with the béchamel.

22. Sprinkle with the remaining Parmigiano.

23. Bake for about 20 minutes, until the whites are set and the top is golden.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Squeeze the spinach thoroughly so it does not release water into the béchamel while baking.

Gobbi alla Perugina

title: Marche Vegetable Fricandò
instructions:
Marche Vegetable Fricandò

Marche-style mixed vegetables with onion, carrots, celery, potatoes, eggplant, peppers, zucchini, and tomatoes slowly stewed together.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

1 onion, coarsely chopped
2 carrots, diced
2 celery stalks, diced
3 1/3 cups diced potatoes
1 eggplant, diced
1 red bell pepper, cut into pieces
1 yellow bell pepper, cut into pieces
2 zucchini, diced
2 cups halved cherry tomatoes
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 cup water or dry white wine, divided
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 tbsp chopped parsley or 1 rosemary sprig

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a very wide skillet.

2. Add the onion.

3. Cook for 5 minutes.

4. Add the carrots and celery.

5. Continue for 5 minutes.

6. Add the potatoes.

7. Cook for 5 minutes.

8. Add the eggplant.

9. After 5 minutes, add the peppers.

10. After another 5 minutes, add the zucchini.

11. Add 1/2 cup water or wine during cooking if the pan becomes dry.

12. Add the cherry tomatoes last.

13. Season with salt and pepper.

14. Cook for another 10 minutes.

15. Add more liquid only if necessary.

16. Turn off the heat.

17. Add the parsley or rosemary.

Service

Serve hot, warm, or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The order in which the vegetables enter the pan matters. The firmest vegetables start first, while tomatoes and zucchini go in last.

title: Marche-style Sautéed Wild Greens
instructions:
Marche-style Sautéed Wild Greens

Mixed field greens boiled and sautéed with garlic, olive oil, and optional chile.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 5 cups fresh spinach
about 5 cups fresh chard
about 3 cups sow thistle greens
about 3 cups chicory
about 3 cups dandelion greens
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil or about 1/3 cup finely chopped lard
2 unpeeled garlic cloves
1 small chile, optional
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Clean all of the greens thoroughly.

2. Wash in several changes of water until completely free of grit.

3. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

4. Boil the greens for 8–12 minutes, until fully tender.

5. Drain.

6. Cool slightly.

7. Squeeze very well.

8. Chop coarsely.

9. Heat the olive oil or melt the lard in a wide skillet.

10. Add the garlic and optional chile.

11. Cook for 1 minute.

12. Add the greens.

13. Sauté and toss for 5–7 minutes.

14. Adjust the salt.

15. Remove the garlic.

Service

Serve very hot.

Chef's note

Squeeze the greens thoroughly before sautéing so the fat seasons them instead of being diluted by cooking water.

title: Ciabotto Abruzzese
instructions:
Ciabotto Abruzzese

Abruzzo vegetable stew with eggplant, zucchini, peppers, potatoes, tomatoes, celery, and carrots.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 eggplant
1 zucchini
3 long sweet peppers
2 potatoes
2 plum tomatoes
1/2 onion
2 celery stalks
2 carrots
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 cups water
1 1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Wash and trim the zucchini and eggplant.

2. Cut them into cubes.

3. Clean the peppers, removing the stems, seeds, and membranes.

4. Cut into pieces.

5. Peel the potatoes and cut into chunks.

6. Peel the tomatoes and cut into pieces.

7. Slice the celery and carrots.

8. Finely chop the onion.

9. Heat the olive oil in an earthenware pot.

10. Add the onion.

11. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.

12. Add all of the vegetables.

13. Pour in the water.

14. Add the salt.

15. Cover.

16. Cook over medium-low heat for about 1 hour, stirring gently every 15 minutes.

17. Remove the lid.

18. Increase the heat and reduce excess liquid for 5–10 minutes, leaving some sauce in the pot.

Service

Serve hot, warm, or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Ciabotto should remain moist and juicy. Reduce the cooking liquid only enough to prevent a watery consistency.
